meta.machine: Intel i5-8500T, 6 cores, 12 GB RAM, no GPU; only the voice service (idle) and local-llm running
meta.server: docker compose local-llm: ollama/ollama:0.40.6, qwen2.5:1.5b (q4_K_M), OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1, OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1, OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=4096, LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_RAM=256
meta.real_request: The voice service's exact first request (POST /v1/chat/completions, stream + stream_options, system + spoken greeting + caller's words + 2 transition tools; 965 prompt tokens), produced by running the voice service's own composition code (WorkflowGraph, compose_system_prompt_for_node, compose_functions_for_node, its template renderer and the OpenAI adapter) inside its container for an agent compiled by ATLAS. ATLAS's warm-up text (system, greeting, tools) was identical for 36 of 36 variable sets across 3 agents.
meta.warmup_request: app.services.llm_warmup.build_warmup_body: same system, greeting and tools, user 'Hello?', max_tokens 1, stream false.
meta.isolation: Every scenario used leads no other scenario used, and the agent's first line contains {{full_name}}, so no two calls share more than ~8 tokens unless warmed.
meta.ttft: Time from sending the real request to the first streamed token, client side.

scenarios.warm_then_real: warm-up finished, 1 s pause, real request
scenarios.warm_classifier_real: warm-up, then the voice service's answer-classifier prompt (a different 800-token prompt), then the real request: the warmed prompt is restored from the server's RAM prompt cache
scenarios.warm_no_tools: warm-up without the tool list, then the real request (what happens when the Start has actions or documents)
scenarios.real_during_warmup_3s: real request sent 3 s after the warm-up started (caller answered and spoke almost at once)
scenarios.warmup_client_timeout_2s: warm-up abandoned by the client after 2 s, real request 12 s later
scenarios.static_prompt_call1_call2: agent without per-lead variables in its prompt, no warm-up: call 1, then call 2 to another lead

meta.previous_measurement_note: Part 1 tuning numbers (local-llm-tuning.json) were taken while a stuck background process used about 1.2 cores; these warm-up numbers were taken after it was stopped.
